subject: comparing densities using the approximate z-test statistic

messages.author: 888b92d1ab888c14
messages.subject: comparing densities using the approximate z-test statistic
parts:
Dear All

I have used the approximate z-test statistic (below) to compare tropical
understorey bird densities in primary and logged forest

D^_1 - D^_2
z = -----------------------------------
sqrt[{se(D^_1)}**2 + {se(D^_2)}**2]

Please can anyone tell me the correct citation for this statistic - it
is described in the archives (email below).

Steve Buckland refers to page 381 - but where? (p381 in the Introduction
to distance sampling (2001) is the bibliography - and neither is this
the statistic described on page 85)

I would like to cite the correct source - any help much appreciated

Claire Mead


Archive email:

> I collected certain data of sika deer using night spotlight counts every
> day along a fixed route in an area. These data include perpendicular
> distance and cluster size of sika deer. I calculated deer density of the
> area using Distance 2.2 (Distance for Win can not work under Japanese
> Windows OS), and now I want to compare deer densities between two
> periods. I tried to compare densities using the 95% confidence
> intervals, but I found the 95% confidence intervals given by Distance
> 2.2 are not symmetric. Should someone tall me how I should statistically
> compare two density estimate results from distance sampling method?

Assessing differences from whether confidence intervals overlap is not
valid whether or not they are symmetric. An approximate z-test is
obtained by taking the statistic

D^_1 - D^_2
z = -----------------------------------
sqrt[{se(D^_1)}**2 + {se(D^_2)}**2]

See p381 of the Distance Sampling book for similar tests. (The book is
available from RUWPA's web pages if you don't have a copy - see below.)

Steve Buckland

example with cluster sizes. It does assume 0 covariance between D1 and
D2 which means they use separate detection functions.--jeff

messages.subject: Re: comparing densities using the approximate z-test statistic
parts:
Hi Claire,

I quickly looked at the index to the 2001 book, and saw that there is a
section 3.6.5, "Estimating change in density". It gives the formula you
quote below (using slightly different notation) as well as the t-based
formula Jeff referred to. Perhaps you could have found this for yourself...

- len

P.S. The page Steve referred to is in the 1993 book, which is available
at http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance.book/ Again, it should not
have taken you more than a few minutes to confirm this.

Claire Mead wrote:
> > Dear All
> >
> > I have used the approximate z-test statistic (below) to compare tropical
> > understorey bird densities in primary and logged forest
> >
> > D^_1 - D^_2
> > z = -----------------------------------
> > sqrt[{se(D^_1)}**2 + {se(D^_2)}**2]
> >
> > Please can anyone tell me the correct citation for this statistic - it
> > is described in the archives (email below).
> >
> > Steve Buckland refers to page 381 - but where? (p381 in the Introduction
> > to distance sampling (2001) is the bibliography - and neither is this
> > the statistic described on page 85)
> >
> > I would like to cite the correct source - any help much appreciated
> >
> > Claire Mead
> >
> >
> > Archive email:
> >
> > > I collected certain data of sika deer using night spotlight counts every
> > > day along a fixed route in an area. These data include perpendicular
> > > distance and cluster size of sika deer. I calculated deer density of the
> > > area using Distance 2.2 (Distance for Win can not work under Japanese
> > > Windows OS), and now I want to compare deer densities between two
> > > periods. I tried to compare densities using the 95% confidence
> > > intervals, but I found the 95% confidence intervals given by Distance
> > > 2.2 are not symmetric. Should someone tall me how I should statistically
> > > compare two density estimate results from distance sampling method?
> >
> > Assessing differences from whether confidence intervals overlap is not
> > valid whether or not they are symmetric. An approximate z-test is
> > obtained by taking the statistic
> >
> > D^_1 - D^_2
> > z = -----------------------------------
> > sqrt[{se(D^_1)}**2 + {se(D^_2)}**2]
> >
> > See p381 of the Distance Sampling book for similar tests. (The book is
> > available from RUWPA's web pages if you don't have a copy - see below.)
> >
> > Steve Buckland
